active_inference_belief.png: Three panels for synthetic alignment-frame evidence: the accusative-frame posterior increases, posterior entropy decreases, and per-update free energy varies. A separately labelled running minimum is an envelope, not the measured trajectory.
alignment_comparison.png: Three schematic mappings of S, A, and P: nominative-accusative groups S with A; ergative-absolutive groups S with P; tripartite gives each a separate label.
case_category_minimal.png: Four coloured role nodes, NOM, ACC, INS, and VOC, linked by selected directed generators. Solid green arrows are admitted by the example specification; dashed red arrows illustrate excluded role promotions.
case_category_standard.png: Eight case-role nodes and hand-authored directed generators, with synthetic weights and separately marked prohibited edges. The graph is a modelling specification, not a grammar inferred from language data.
complexity_comparison.png: Horizontal grouped bars compare total boxes, word boxes, and cups for ten explicitly constructed sentence examples. Row labels identify the example and lexical box contents; counts concern the implemented diagrams.
composition_triangle.png: A triangular path from NOM through ACC to DAT, with a direct solid arrow labelled h equals g composed with f. The direct arrow denotes the composite path.
daif_belief_trajectory.png: The ordered synthetic evidence updates concentrate posterior mass on NOM. Separate panels show role probabilities, decreasing entropy, and total variation between successive stored beliefs; the first undefined change is displayed as zero.
daif_erp_predictions.png: Left: hand-selected role weights versus model prediction errors. Right: negative N400-inspired and positive P600-inspired amplitude proxies by role, explicitly labelled as uncalibrated model units.
daif_free_energy_convergence.png: Synthetic filter updates show per-update free energy. A companion panel plots KL from the predicted prior and negative expected log likelihood; their plotted sum equals the free-energy trajectory.
discocirc_entity_persistence.png: Three sentence schematics reuse the supplied names Alice and Bob. A lower ribbon tracks Alice through NOM, ACC, NOM and Bob through ACC, NOM, then absence; no inferred coreference or semantic state update is shown.
discopy_composition.png: Two native DisCoPy renderings show the tensor of Alice, chases, and Bob before and after attaching noun-type cups; the sentence output wire remains.
discopy_discocirc_discourse.png: Native diagrams for Alice chases Bob and Bob runs appear in parallel. Bob is a repeated lexical label; the combined output is a tensor of sentence outputs.
discopy_ditransitive.png: A native typed diagram for Alice gives Bob a book contracts three noun arguments against the verb slots and leaves one sentence wire.
discopy_multilingual.png: English, Latin-inspired, and Japanese-inspired lexical substitutions share one normalized transitive diagram template. The displayed order is a template convention, not a verified surface grammar for all three languages.
discopy_passive.png: A native diagram for Bob is chased by Alice uses a separately assigned passive predicate type and two noun cups, leaving sentence output s.
discopy_sentence_progression.png: Intransitive, transitive, and passive typed examples are shown side by side. Arrows separate examples and do not assert a semantics-preserving rewrite between sentences.
discopy_snake.png: A left cup-cap zigzag, straight identity wire, and right zigzag are equated in the specified rigid diagram calculus.
discopy_three_sentence_discourse.png: Three independent native diagrams for Alice chases Bob, Bob fears Alice, and Alice smiles are tensored together. Shared names do not constitute a state-update circuit.
discopy_transitive.png: A larger native pregroup diagram contracts determiners, modifiers, and two noun arguments in the sentence about an agent intercepting a payload. Lexical types are supplied explicitly.
discourse_string_diagram.png: Two vertical entity tracks labelled Alice and Bob intersect sentence boxes for chases and runs. Role dots record supplied NOM and ACC assignments across these sentence schematics.
enriched_hom_matrix.png: An eight-by-eight heatmap prints hand-selected similarity values between case roles, with unit diagonal. It is labelled a synthetic candidate matrix because some multiplicative composition inequalities fail.
experiment_calibration.png: Empirical coverage of synthetic discrete outcomes is compared with the exact cumulative probability at each model quantile. A separate error panel shows replicate uncertainty relative to this discrete target; nominal quantile levels are not treated as exact attainable coverage.
experiment_filtering.png: Synthetic filtering and ablation results across independently seeded replicates. Points summarize replicate outcomes; labelled intervals quantify simulation uncertainty under the supplied model, with no linguistic measurements.
experiment_sensitivity.png: Prespecified parameter sweeps show paired changes relative to each declared baseline using common random inputs. Every arm is displayed with pointwise simulation uncertainty; intervals do not correct for simultaneous comparisons.
fluid_s_volition_landscape.png: A synthetic logistic surface maps hand-selected volition and agentivity coordinates to an ERG-labelled probability. Verb labels are illustrative coordinates; a dashed line marks probability one-half.
functor_alignment.png: Two role-label graphs illustrate nominative-accusative and ergative-absolutive groupings. Dashed correspondence arrows show a chosen relabelling between the expanded diagrams, including merged labels.
monoidal_functor_security.png: A chosen role map is paired with a yes/no matrix for role separation and edge existence. The title identifies a synthetic policy, not a proof of monoidal functor laws.
pregroup_reduction_unpacking.png: Four pedagogical panels show lexical types for Alice chases Bob, their tensor product, two noun cups, and a sentence-meaning box with remaining output type s.
quantum_povm_probabilities.png: A bar chart shows Born-rule outcome probabilities for a supplied diagonal density and crisp case projectors. NOM has the largest mass, ACC and DAT share smaller equal masses, and the remaining labels have zero mass.
security_type_violations.png: Two supplied-label data-flow examples compare an admitted trace with an attempted webpage-to-tool authority promotion. PASS and FAIL refer to the example policy; the hand-selected score is explicitly not runtime enforcement.
snake_equation_unpacking.png: A pedagogical cup-cap zigzag is paired with a straight identity wire and the two typed duality identities. The equality applies inside the specified categorical calculus.
string_diagram_discocat.png: A native schematic places Alice, Bob, and chases in separate boxes. Noun and sentence wires and dashed role connections illustrate supplied metadata rather than an executable cup reduction.
syntactic_case_panel.png: Eight hand-authored dependency-style sketches cover intransitive, transitive, ditransitive, passive, schematic ergative, benefactive, relative-clause, and causative constructions. The last two explicitly state that no formal derivation is supplied.
